correctness.rationale: Direct Gram integration gives the signed inverse formula (1). Every relevant bi-infinite Green coefficient solves the piecewise constant Jacobi recurrence with exponential tails; exact SymPy identities validate (2),(3) and their sign factorizations. The row-stochastic Neumann contraction 1/2, uniform distance decay, and rank-two resolvent identity prove the periodic limit exists, while the two witness rows give strict lower bounds. Checker was executed successfully on current package sources; finite tests were not misused as an infinite proof. The full limiting norm is not claimed explicitly.

originality.rationale: Comparison by implication finds prior general Gram-kernel identities and uniform bounds, but not a determination of the strict isolated-defect sign law for every ratio. The two-block Franklin limit, the equal-cell and alternating-periodic formulas, and smooth-input supercloseness do not cover the one-exception asymptotic. Originality remains conditional on accessible sources, with explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: Other classical spline sources or unindexed results may have already derived an equivalent one-cell limit; several cited primary sources were inspected only in relevant sections.
The explicit lower witnesses do not determine the full optimum or all maximizing sites, so they must not be advertised as exact sharp norm formulas.

value.rationale: This is a universal and non-obvious sign law for a canonical local mesh perturbation: the unique uniform ratio has limiting norm 2 whereas any fixed nonunit single-cell ratio gives strict amplification; the previously derived microscopic alternating mesh behaves in the opposite direction. Explicit analytic positive margins cover both short and long anomalies and a nontrivial extreme-ratio lower bound. This informs worst-case stability of local remeshing rather than merely cataloguing numerical instances.
